section_summary: This section comprises documents from decimal file 894.43 covering Japanese political, cultural, patriotic, and bilateral friendship societies between 1932 and 1939 (including a 1923 retrospective report). It details the membership and nationalistic tendencies of youth and reservist associations, the establishment and platform of Kenzo Adachi's Kokumin Domei, and the founding and propaganda activities of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai), including its planned New York branch at Rockefeller Center. In addition, the file records the functions and bilateral goodwill initiatives of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo, the Japan-America Society of Kwansai, the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society, and the Philippine-Japan Society.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet and attached extract from Tokyo Despatch No. 588 reporting on reactionary tendencies in Japanese youth organizations and national defence associations.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet records an extract from Despatch No. 588 (originally filed under 894.00/385) concerning reactionary movements and national defence organizations in Japan. The extract details the membership and objectives of groups including the Imperial Reservists Association, Young Men's Associations, Young Men's Training Institutes, and Young Women's Associations, noting their ethical and military instruction. It also lists three patriotic national defence associations: the Navy Association (Kaigun Kyokai), the Sea Defence Association (Kaibo Gikai), and the National Defence Association (Kokubo Gikai).
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Despatch No. 588 with Extract regarding Reactionary Tendencies in Japanese Youth and National Defence Organizations

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 180 concerning the Kokumin Domei formed by Kenzo Adachi.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 180, dated September 20, 1932 (cross-referenced to 894.00/842). It notes that the despatch reports on the Kokumin Domei, a new political party organized by Kenzo Adachi following his separation from the Minseito.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 180 regarding Kokumin Domei

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the formation, platform, and policy of Kenzo Adachi's new political party, the Kokumin Domei, with enclosed translations of party documents.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the establishment of the Kokumin Domei (National League or People's League) led by former Home Minister Kenzo Adachi following the collapse of the Wakatsuki Cabinet. The despatch analyzes the party's influence in the Diet, where thirty Lower House members defected from the Minseito to join it, securing an absolute majority for the Seiyukai. Enclosed are English translations of the party's declaration of principles, three-point platform, and thirteen-point provisional outline of policy, which advocates state economic control, judicial independence, and a Japan-Manchukuo economic bloc.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 180: The Kokumin Domei, A New Political Organization

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 798 regarding the newly established Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: This document file note records the receipt of Despatch No. 798 from Tokyo, dated May 22, 1934. It notes that the despatch encloses a descriptive pamphlet regarding the Society for International Cultural Relations, organized under the presidency of Prince Fumimaro Konoe.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 798 regarding The Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a prospectus pamphlet and press report on the inaugural diplomatic reception of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai).
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits literature describing the newly organized Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai), headed by Prince Fumimaro Konoe, and reports on an inaugural tea party held for the Tokyo diplomatic corps at the Peers' Club. The despatch notes that the society seeks to promote Japanese culture abroad in order to offset foreign hostility aroused by Japan's aggressive foreign policy. Enclosures include the society's published prospectus and ten-point activity program, a list of officers, an exhibition list of Suzuki Harunobu color prints from Shigekichi Mihara's collection, and a report from The Japan Advertiser featuring speeches by Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa and Belgian Ambassador Baron Albert de Bassompierre.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 798: Transmitting Pamphlets Describing the Proposed Activities of The Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 1245 regarding the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai.
subfiles.summary: Wallace T. Turner of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs provides a brief summary of Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 1245. He notes that the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai is an incorporated semi-official foundation receiving government subsidies from the Foreign Office and large corporate contributions totaling about one million yen. The memorandum highlights that the society, chaired by Count Aisuke Kabayama, seeks to bring cultural information activities under unified direction.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1245 on the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai

subfiles.about: Despatch analyzing the organization, finances, leadership, and cultural propaganda work of the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai).
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides a detailed report on the first year of operations of the Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai, incorporated on April 14, 1934. He outlines its financial backing, which includes a 300,000 yen subsidy from the Japanese Foreign Office and private corporate support from Mitsui and Mitsubishi bringing total funds to around one million yen. The report discusses its leadership under Count Aisuke Kabayama and Baron Ino Dan, its public library in Marunouchi, and specific projects such as assisting American legal scholar Dr. John Henry Wigmore and hosting the Garden Club of America, advising that American scholars might utilize its resources advantageously.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1245: Society for International Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum noting the Tokyo Embassy's transmittal of the new Japanese quarterly magazine NIPPON.
subfiles.summary: Wallace T. Turner informs Eugene H. Dooman of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs about Tokyo Despatch No. 1300 transmitting a copy of NIPPON. The memorandum notes that the quarterly illustrates actual life in modern Japan and works in close cooperation with the Society for International Cultural Relations. Turner characterizes the society as a semi-official propaganda agency subsidized by the Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1300 and the Quarterly Magazine NIPPON

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting issue No. 3 of NIPPON, an illustrated multilingual quarterly magazine published in Tokyo for foreign distribution.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits the April 1935 issue (No. 3) of NIPPON, an illustrated quarterly published in English, French, German, and Spanish. Grew reports that the magazine works closely with the Society for International Cultural Relations and features a statement of the society's activities and accomplishments on page 8. The despatch notes that circulation remains modest and supplements the embassy's earlier Despatch No. 1245.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1300: Sample Copy of New Quarterly, NIPPON

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet recording remarks by Marquis Tokugawa regarding the formation of a society to foster cultural ties with the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1363, dated June 24, 1935 (originally filed under 032 Philippine Athletic Teams/1). It records that Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa informed Ambassador Grew of the recent organization of a separate society dedicated to developing cultural relations between Japan and the Philippine Islands.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 1363 regarding Philippine Cultural Relations

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 2974 on Count Kabayama's mission to establish a New York branch of the Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Schuler of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs summarizes Tokyo Despatch No. 2974 regarding Count Aisuke Kabayama's voyage to the United States. The memorandum reports that Kabayama intends to set up a branch of the Society for International Cultural Relations in Rockefeller Center, New York, under the direction of Tamon Maeda of the Tokyo Asahi. It also notes Kabayama's anticipated arrival in Washington around June 20 and his stay at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 2974 and Culture Society Branch for New York

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Count Aisuke Kabayama's voyage to the United States to establish a New York branch and library for the Society for International Cultural Relations.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Count Aisuke Kabayama sailed on the Hikawa Maru to establish a branch office and library for the Society for International Cultural Relations in Rockefeller Center, New York. The office will provide research facilities, answer cultural inquiries, and arrange professor and student exchanges, with Tamon Maeda designated to take charge in autumn 1938. The despatch also notes Kabayama's plan to attend the Princeton graduation of Prince Konoe's son, and encloses a clipping from The Japan Advertiser quoting Kabayama and General Secretary Setsuichi Aoki regarding the society's international operations.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2974: Culture Society Branch for New York

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Japan-America Society under decimal classification 894.43.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State case file jacket (Form 1-1235) creating the subject heading 'JAPAN-AMERICA SOCIETY' under decimal file 894.43. The jacket is dated June 20, 1932, and contains instructions prohibiting the disarrangement or defacing of documents preserved within the file.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 Japan-America Society

subfiles.about: Consular despatch from Kobe reporting on the founding, officers, and aims of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai.
subfiles.summary: Erle R. Dickover, American Consul in Charge at Kobe, reports on the inaugural meeting of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai held at the Osaka Hotel on February 26, 1923. Formed by leading Japanese business figures and American residents of Kobe, Osaka, and Kyoto, the society aims to promote bilateral friendship, welcome distinguished visitors, and foster mutual understanding. The despatch lists the elected officers, headed by President Kojiro Matsukata, and explains that American membership is being built selectively to avoid disproportionate missionary or radical influence.
subfiles.title: Despatch regarding Organization of the Japan-America Society of Kwansai

subfiles.about: Consular despatch transmitting a commemorative booklet on the official visit of Consuls Dickover and Donovan to Wakayama Prefecture.
keywords: Japan-America Society of the City of Wakayama
subfiles.summary: American Consul Howard Donovan reports on the visit he and Consul Erle R. Dickover made to Wakayama Prefecture on December 5, 1931, to attend the inaugural meeting of the Japan-America Society of the City of Wakayama. Donovan emphasizes that this was the first visit paid to Wakayama Prefecture by any official representative of the United States government. The despatch encloses copies of a descriptive booklet published by the local society and mentions an anticipated follow-up visit.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 19: Visit of Consuls Dickover and Donovan to Wakayama Prefecture, Japan

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 476 regarding Prince Iyesato Tokugawa's prospective visits to the United States.
subfiles.summary: This document file note records Tokyo Despatch No. 476, dated July 19, 1933 (cross-referenced to 033.9411 Tokugawa, Iyesato/1). It concerns the travels to the United States in 1933 and 1934 of Prince Iyesato Tokugawa, President of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 476 regarding Prince Iyesato Tokugawa's Visit to the United States

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum calling attention to Viscount Kaneko's letter setting forth his views on the 1924 Exclusion Act.
subfiles.summary: Laurence E. Salisbury of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs writes a brief note recommending the reading of Viscount Kentaro Kaneko's letter to the America-Japan Society enclosed with Tokyo Despatch No. 576. The memorandum notes that the letter articulates Kaneko's views regarding the American Immigration Act of 1924 (the Exclusion Act).
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Viscount Kaneko's Letter on the Exclusion Act

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting historical Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo for preservation in the Department archives.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits nine issues of the Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo for permanent retention in the State Department archives. He notes that four issues containing Lincoln Essay Contest entries were out of print. Grew specifically highlights Special Bulletin No. 1, which contains Viscount Kentaro Kaneko's letter of resignation from the society's presidency following the passage of the U.S. Immigration Act of 1924, together with responses from prominent Americans.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 576: Transmitting Special Bulletins of The America-Japan Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department instruction acknowledging receipt of Tokyo Despatch No. 576 and confirming placement of the bulletins in the Department Library.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges receipt of Ambassador Grew's Despatch No. 576 of November 9, 1933. The instruction informs the embassy that the transmitted Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo have been placed in the Library of the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Instruction acknowledging Despatch No. 576 on Special Bulletins of the America-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum evaluating the speeches published in America-Japan Society Bulletin No. 14.
subfiles.summary: Eugene H. Dooman comments on Tokyo Despatch No. 884 transmitting Special Bulletin No. 14 of the America-Japan Society. Dooman notes that the Department has already received Ambassador Grew's speeches and remarks that the other addresses in the publication are not particularly interesting.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 884 and America-Japan Society Speeches

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting Special Bulletin No. 14 containing principal speeches delivered at America-Japan Society gatherings during 1933-1934.
subfiles.summary: Referring to his earlier Despatch No. 576, Ambassador Grew transmits a copy of Special Bulletin No. 14 (May 1934) of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo. The bulletin compiles the principal addresses delivered at the dinners and luncheons held by the society during the fiscal year ending April 30, 1934.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 884: Transmitting Special Bulletins of The America-Japan Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet regarding a proposed dinner by the America-Japan Society for the visiting U.S. Congressional delegation.
subfiles.summary: This document file note records a letter from Takashi Komatsu referred to the State Department for acknowledgment, cross-referenced to 033.1111b Congressional Delegation/38. The note details the desire of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo to host a dinner or luncheon in honor of the Vice President of the United States and visiting members of the Congressional delegation in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Letter regarding Proposed Dinner for U.S. Congressional Delegation

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 3542 and luncheon speeches by General Burnett and Admiral Nomura.
subfiles.summary: An internal memorandum of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Political Adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck reviews Tokyo Despatch No. 3542. It notes that the despatch encloses speeches delivered by Brigadier-General Charles Burnett and Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura at an America-Japan Society luncheon on December 12, 1938. The memorandum observes that the addresses express familiar sentiments regarding Japanese fortitude and need not be read.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 3542 and Speeches of General Burnett and Admiral Nomura

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a press report of speeches delivered by General Charles Burnett, Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura, and Count Aisuke Kabayama at the America-Japan Society.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits an account from The Japan Advertiser of an America-Japan Society luncheon on December 12, 1938, welcoming Brigadier-General Charles Burnett, Chief of the Bureau of Insular Affairs and former U.S. military attaché. Presided over by Count Aisuke Kabayama in the absence of Prince Iyesato Tokugawa, the gathering heard Admiral Kichisaburo Nomura compare Japan's aspirations in China to the American Monroe Doctrine while cautioning that Japanese diplomacy 'cries too much.' General Burnett praised Japan's courage in past crises, and Count Kabayama reviewed Burnett's career and relief leadership following the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3542: Speech of Brigadier-General Charles Burnett at America-Japan Society, December 12, 1938

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo under decimal classification 894.43.
keywords: International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo
subfiles.summary: A Department of State case file jacket (Form 1-1235) creating the subject heading 'THE INTERNATIONAL GOODWILL KOI-NOBORI SOCIETY OF TOKYO' under decimal file 894.43 KOI-NOBORI. The jacket is dated April 22, 1935, and carries standard archival preservation notices.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 The International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo

subfiles.about: Letter from the Boy Scouts of America inquiring about the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo, transmitting an enclosed appeal from Soichi Saito.
keywords: International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo
subfiles.summary: E. H. Vitalius, Secretary to Chief Scout Executive James E. West of the Boy Scouts of America, requests information from the Department of State regarding the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society of Tokyo and asks whether it is proper to cooperate with its efforts. Vitalius encloses a letter dated April 5, 1935, from Soichi Saito, Executive Secretary of the Tokyo society, which transmitted a pair of traditional carp flags (koi-nobori) as tokens of friendship from Japanese boys. Saito's letter requests that the flags be displayed in a public park, Y.M.C.A., or department store to promote international goodwill among youth.
subfiles.title: Letter from Boy Scouts of America regarding International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society

subfiles.about: State Department letter providing biographical information on Soichi Saito, signatory of the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society.
subfiles.summary: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Assistant Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, replies to E. H. Vitalius's inquiry of April 22 regarding the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society. Hamilton states that while the Department lacks information concerning the society itself, Japanese biographical records identify its signatory, Soichi Saito, as Secretary General of the Federation of Young Men's Christian Associations of Japan and a prominent delegate to the Institute of Pacific Relations conferences in Honolulu, Kyoto, and Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Letter to Boy Scouts of America regarding the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society

subfiles.about: Letter from the Boy Scouts of America expressing appreciation for State Department information on Soichi Saito, accompanied by Scouting literature.
subfiles.summary: E. H. Vitalius of the Boy Scouts of America thanks Maxwell M. Hamilton for providing biographical background on Soichi Saito and the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society. Accompaniments to the letter include promotional leaflets and order forms detailing Boy Scouts of America handicraft publications and official patrol leader handbooks.
subfiles.title: Letter from Boy Scouts of America acknowledging Information on Soichi Saito (with Attachments)

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Philippine-Japan Society under decimal classification 894.43.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State case file jacket (Form 1-1235) creating the subject file 'The Philippine-Japan Society: Inauguration of-, purporting to promote and strengthen the cultural relations between the two countries' under decimal classification 894.43. The jacket is dated September 5, 1935.
subfiles.title: File Jacket: 894.43 Philippine-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum analyzing the diplomatic significance of the newly established Philippine-Japan Society.
subfiles.summary: Wallace T. Turner submits an internal memorandum to Eugene H. Dooman regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1457. Turner highlights the embassy's evaluation that the inauguration of the Philippine-Japan Society reflects expanding Japanese interest in the Philippines stimulated by impending political changes and the approaching establishment of the Philippine Commonwealth.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 1457 on Formation of the Philippine-Japan Society

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the inauguration of the Philippine-Japan Society under Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa, transmitting an enclosed newspaper report.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville reports on the founding of the Philippine-Japan Society in Tokyo under the presidency of Marquis Yorisada Tokugawa, identifying it as a reflection of heightened Japanese interest in the Philippine Islands prior to their political transition. The despatch encloses an account from the English edition of the Tokyo Nichi Nichi reporting on the inaugural meeting held on August 23, 1935, at Tokugawa's Azabu residence. The article details the society's leadership, including Vice-President Viscount Nagakage Okabe, and lists attending Japanese parliamentarians and officials as well as prominent Philippine backers such as Manuel Quezon and Jose Abad Santos.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1457: Philippine-Japan Society Created at Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department subject jacket establishing the file for the Shiunso under decimal classification 894.43.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 43 regarding an open letter from the reactionary Shiunso to the Lytton Commission.
keywords: League of Nations Commission of Enquiry
subfiles.summary: This document file note records Tokyo Despatch No. 43, dated July 7, 1932 (cross-referenced to 793.94 Commission/312). It indexes an open letter addressed to the League of Nations Commission of Enquiry (the Lytton Commission) by the Shiunso, described as a small reactionary Japanese organization, reiterating Japan's policy regarding China and Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Despatch No. 43 regarding Open Letter from the Shiunso

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum recommending an article by the Japanese Foreign Minister containing recollections of the late diplomat Enjiro Yamaza.
subfiles.summary: Eugene H. Dooman writes a memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 619 of December 21, 1933, which transmitted a translation of a magazine article by Foreign Minister Koki Hirota. The article recounts recollections of the late Japanese diplomat Enjiro Yamaza. Dooman recommends reading the article for its valuable insight into the background and character of Foreign Minister Hirota.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Despatch No. 619 and Foreign Minister's Recollections of Diplomat Yamaza
